analysis.title: GS Futures Global Bonds CTA - Market Update - November 16, 2026
key_insights: GS's model simulates CTAs (trend-following funds) having covered nearly $100mm DV01 of their bond shorts over the past month. The model has now reverted to negative trend, with 26 of 27 modeled trend signals negative.
GS forecasts CTAs will net sell global duration this week. The baseline flow forecast is $6.5mm DV01 of global duration sold.
Over the next month GS estimates CTAs will sell around $42mm DV01 of duration. If realized, this would re-establish half of the net short position they had just covered.

US and Germany differ on short-term trend signals. In the US, all short-term signals are more than 1.0 standard deviation away from flipping positive. In Germany, all short-term signals are within 0.5 standard deviations of flipping.
risk_factors: The figures come from backtested and simulated models. GS gives no assurance the strategy would have operated in the past as the analysis shows.
The note is a desk message from FICC and Equities Futures Sales Strats and is not a Global Investment Research report.
vol_and_positioning: GS simulated CTA positioning in global bonds: nearly $100mm DV01 of shorts covered over the past month, with 26 of 27 trend signals now negative.
Forecast CTA flow: sell $6.5mm DV01 of global duration this week and about $42mm DV01 over the next month, which would rebuild half of the net short just covered.
US short-term trend signals sit more than 1.0 standard deviation from flipping positive. German short-term signals sit within 0.5 standard deviations, so Bunds are more likely to flip.
